title: Culture of Gratitude 1/6: The World
why: Series opener. Names the gap: gratitude elsewhere is a daily habit; here it shows up on a few days a year.
en:
In many nations, a veteran hears "Thank you for your service" at the shop counter, the hospital desk and the airport gate. Every single day.

In Bharat, our respect for the uniform runs deeper than anyone's. But it shows up on a few days of the year, and then it goes quiet.

A soldier gives his best years to the nation. The nation's thank-you should last his whole life.

That is the Culture of Gratitude. Rakshak ID is built to make it visible, at every counter, every day.

Part 1 of 6. Follow @rakshakid for the series.

title: Culture of Gratitude 2/6: The Why
why: The family's sacrifice. Brings in Veer Naris, Rakshak Naris, children and parents.
en:
Why should a soldier's thank-you last only one day?

A new posting every few years. Children changing schools again and again. A spouse holding the home together through every silence. Parents who sent their son to the border.

Service is never a solo act. The whole family serves. So the thank-you must reach all of them: the Veteran, the Veer Nari, the Rakshak Nari, the children and the parents. And it must last a lifetime.
